title: Wide cross-platform discovery pass 45
summary: Personally inspect 42 roots: add 38 projects and record one duplicate, two exclusions and one deferred target-toolchain claim.
notes: Root personally ran 48 cross-platform searches yielding 474 hits and 471 distinct repository URLs, inspected 42 selected roots and prepared 38 additions plus four explicit non-promotions. Search covered classic home computers, consoles, handhelds and tool/project types; additions include native applications, source continuations, language runtimes, compilers, debuggers, binary analysis, media/disk/ROM tools, translation source and Williams WPC pinball analysis. Broad search does not imply every platform is exhausted or every project category added. No discovery worker used; no upstream software, ROM, firmware, installer, network helper or disk modification executed. Catalogues refreshed at 1f569ee639548544a9a706327ac449fbd3b21139; activity history is cached, so live trusted-main validation is required. Ingestion observations: title/lineage dedup caught retrokit rename after URL screening called it new; stable GitHub repository IDs must follow redirects. Implementation language differs from GitHub majority-language statistics (BasicV2/romusage). Missing or empty READMEs can coexist with substantive code, while a template README contains no feature evidence. Extensionless BBC BASIC source is not binary-only. PC Engines APU is a vendor collision, music assemblers compile bytecode rather than CPU instructions, Apple II programmer firmware executes on AVR, and a tentative WonderSwan compiler may still expose inherited PC/ELKS targets. Distinguish native CPU/OS minima from historical performance anecdotes. File tools can modify on open/repair/flush, and read/write/conversion support varies by format and version. Preserve raw-data prerequisites and version limits: POKEY dumps rather than SAP, SEQ64 V2 sequences rather than whole ROMs, mono-only ADPCM, DSi predecryption, limited CoCo geometry. Source defects and stated corruption risks are retained, not promoted to safe editor claims. Translation downloaders are not translation-development tools. Music reconstruction can preserve historical player bugs; fixing arithmetic is not automatic original fidelity. AI evidence remains scoped to explicit disclosure, not presence of an MCP frontend.

sources.reason: Source-backed tests cover socket lifecycle, I/O, DNS, descriptor transfer and benchmarks. Loopback and host-assisted network tiers differ; skipped privileged operations are not passes.

Implements partition layouts, FFS/OFS/PFS3/FAT32 file operations, floppies, LHA and artwork decoding. Filesystem mounting includes allocator bitmap repair bookkeeping; inspection should not be presumed side-effect-free without checking device/write/flush mode.

GadTools partition/format utility with device-liveness classification and fail-safe treatment when boot device is unknown. RDB handling derives from amitools; existing host tests compare layout output, not every live disk operation.
Source examples progress from TOS programs and console input to A-Line graphics. Demonstration collection, not reconstructed commercial games or a full SDK.
Editor has phrase/chain/song management, keyboard interaction and player components. Low hand travel is a design goal; fast playback and low RAM use are explicitly not current goals.
Java BASIC runtime and cross-compiler with 6502 assembler/emulator and script-language backends. BASIC is parsed into host objects rather than residing as original tokenized code in emulated RAM.

Assembles and decompiles Fuxoft music language, including loops/calls and per-voice state. Decompilation is explicitly not universally round-trippable; some historical tracks are invalid yet happened to play.

Web/desktop quantization, dithering and exports for classic CPC and Plus, including per-line palettes and tilesets. Mode pen-budget code constrains reserved/transparency pens; 4096 available colours does not mean4096 simultaneous pens.
Native tests exercise lower or upper16KiB under several display modes, looping until error or BREAK. Targets mode-dependent RAM symptoms, not proof of all possible hardware faults.
Single extensionless source file embeds assembler in BBC BASIC and installs OSWORD E0 transfer handling. Includes Tube claiming, parameter layout and presence/unload operations.
USB CDC firmware and hardware design implement block reads/writes for ROM/EEPROM devices. Apple II is the ROM context; firmware executes on ATmega32U4, not6502.
Source implements CFG/SSA/C-generation experiments with a udis86 wrapper. Author explicitly calls it broken/incomplete toy work, not a working arbitrary-DOS porting pipeline.
Continuation of released Compass source with editor, monitor and debugger, assembled via Nestor80. Source-supported improvements are distinct from original authorship.
Scans standard MFM_DISK sector ID/data marks and rewrites incorrect CRCs. Assumes standard byte-aligned layout; not general flux recovery or deliberate copy-protection preservation.
Converts POKEY dumps into transcription-oriented MIDI, not SAP files directly. Slides become retriggered notes; noise/high-pass effects are unhandled, so this is not a faithful sound renderer.
Integrated8KiB monitor/assembler source with BASIC-facing facilities and cartridge/PRG packaging. Real implementation despite absent root README.
Native Small-C compiler with cross-target runtimes. Explicit restricted subset: no structs/unions/floats/typedef/casts, single-level pointers and one-dimensional arrays. Not a full ANSI C compiler.
Library handles resampling/filtering and BRR samples for SNES audio. Separate GUI is linked but not included as a claimed library feature.
Palette browsing/editing supports whole ROMs and split data, with binary/assembly-related UI. Data tool, not game decompilation.
Implements palette/tile/ROM data editing, but README warns of source-data corruption and unfinished compression writing, text editing and attribute rendering. Not a safe complete editor.
Estimates usage from map/NOI/IHX/CDB files or ROMs, with overlaps, manual areas and bank templates. SMS/Game Gear rules are GBDK-specific, not arbitrary-ROM structure recovery.
Translation source includes script, art, font codecs and patch-building tools. Modifies original ROM rather than reconstructing the entire original game.
V2 converts MIDI, textual MUS and binary COM/ASEQ/M64 music language with commands/loops and control flow. It no longer loads whole ROMs; legacyV1.5 serves that workflow.
Edits object placement, carrier motion, gravity and level metadata, with collision display and OBJ export. USA1.0/1.1 supported; European support is future intent.
Converts wave audio to DCA/ADPCM or PCM with mono/stereo and length/rate controls. Defaults can downsample and mix to mono to fit a single AICA channel.
AICA/Yamaha ADPCM to WAV utility with configurable header skip and sample rate. Designed around Magic the Gathering assets; explicitly excludes stereo even where extensions match.
Builds C overlays at configured RAM locations, supports runtime patching via emulator integration and disc/xdelta assembly. It assists mods, not automatic full-game C recovery.

Windows GUI and Python bakers convert user-supplied disc data for a separate PSP engine. Audio path treats PS2 VAG and PC PCM differently and excludes speech/radio/mission banks from the selected bake; not a full playable port itself.
Builds/unpacks DS ROMs from components with ARM7/ARM9, overlay, banner and alignment handling. Packaging is not decompilation of game logic.
Wraps DS binaries/addresses into an ELF template for Ghidra/IDA. DSi modcrypt must already be removed; converter is not a decrypter or recovered source project.
Edits GCM/RARC/BTI/J3D/JPC and compression formats, plus DOL offset inspection. Can create RARC but not new GCM/JPC; BMG scope is currently Wind Waker only.
Source parses MusyX samples, macros and instrument/ADSR structures. Empty root README and template ReadMe.txt do not mean source absent; feature scope is taken conservatively from implementation.
Displays keyboard/mouse/two-joystick input through IOCS for real X68000 or X68000Z mapping checks. Does not establish electrical compatibility of every adapter.
Direct-threaded Forth with cross-assembler/compiler sources and fast-RAM primitives. Library is not fully vetted; author warns some ITC-derived assumptions can crash DTC code.
Formats, lists, copies and removes files in161280-byte35-track linear disk images. No fsck/repair capability yet; not arbitrary CoCo/OS-9 filesystem coverage.
Host tools list/copy/remove/format/check CP/M images, with optional libdsk and filesystem definitions. This is genuinely CP/M support, unlike same-acronym CMake wrappers.

Metadata-guided ROM disassembly/reassembly, fingerprint label transfer, comparisons, DMD decoding and checksum tools target WPC/WPC-S/WPC95. Heuristic tables and matches remain hypotheses; roundtrip is a build check, not semantic completeness.
Implements instruction, SSA, block and code-generation modules with explicit origin/entry/MMIO inputs. Not a complete automatic game-port generator or proof of recoverable indirect control flow.

Already tracked as retrokit-le-lx-ghidra-toolkit under nemo22/retrokit. Old API redirects to repository1418067423, identical to the selected new owner. Preserve renamed-owner identity instead of creating another project.
PC Engines is the APU network-appliance vendor here, not NEC PC Engine. Script downloads/flashes modern appliance firmware and reboots; not retro console tooling.

Implementation is a bulk downloader/launcher setup for prepatched game libraries and emulators, not a translation patch authoring tool or source reconstruction. No independent reverse-engineering or format implementation established in inspected scripts.

Description proposes a WonderSwan C compiler, but inspected README/Makefile/compiler driver document inherited BCC/ELKS/PC8086 targets. Retain lead until WonderSwan-specific ABI/runtime/ROM output is evidenced; do not label a complete target toolchain from the repository name.
